comparisons.finding: A=7.3; F=6.7; overall=6.9. The large artifact establishes a strong focal point, but Download, video and invitation receive nearly equal treatment. At 200%, Download remains visible near the bottom; its supporting format line competes with the action. Successful image export and handled video error have supplied production evidence; successful video does not. Component scores [hierarchy, typography, surfaces, clarity, feedback, accessibility]: artifact [8,6,8,8,N/A,6]—recognizable preview, small embedded qualification; Download row [6,7,8,8,8,6]—accurate label and proven export, weak primary emphasis; video row [6,7,8,6,6,6]—offers an uncertain capability before explaining failure; invitation row [6,7,8,8,N/A,6]—helpful exclusion copy; close/quota header [6,7,8,6,N/A,6]—quota distracts from sharing and the icon lacks a visible text label. A=8.0; F=6.7; overall=7.2, provisional composition grade. Best Share balance: the poster leads directly to a dominant Download button, and visible privacy copy explains what leaves the app. At 200%, the button appears earlier than in B or C; privacy continues below the initial viewport. The smaller poster makes its embedded words harder to inspect, and the poetic title is less direct than 'Share this glimpse.' Download's 5 reflects the supplied truthful no-file feedback, not successful export. Shipping requires real export, result/error handling and implemented secondary tools.

A=7.3; F=6.3; overall=6.7, provisional composition grade. At normal size, the compact editorial arrangement makes privacy, invitation, reminder and video unavailability easy to discover. A=6.3; F=6.0; overall=6.1. The illustration and prediction preserve continuity with the reading, but dominate a screen whose current purpose is explanation. A=8.0; F=8.0; overall=8.0, provisional composition grade. Best Why composition by a narrow margin. At 200%, reasoning remains readable, but its long paragraph pushes every closed section below the initial view. A=7.3; F=5.7; overall=6.3, provisional composition grade. The editorial rail and section navigation give the page structure, but the initial view lacks the prediction context present in A and B. At 200%, the navigation visibly clips the Assumptions label, while the inset content rail narrows an already constrained reading column. All evidence may remain reachable by scrolling; the defect is navigation legibility and avoidable reading cost. Component scores [hierarchy, typography, surfaces, clarity, feedback, accessibility]: back/brand header [8,8,8,8,N/A,7]; page title [8,8,8,7,N/A,8]; section-navigation links [6,5,8,6,5,4]—clipped at enlargement, similar underlines do not identify a current section; reasoning/rail [7,7,8,7,N/A,6]; answers [8,8,8,8,N/A,7]; assumptions [7,8,8,7,7,7]. Working section links are supplied evidence, but destination focus and enlarged navigation reachability need checks. Clipping a redundant section link does not establish that essential evidence is inaccessible.

reason: Share A gives the clearest sequence from preview to Download to privacy, with the earliest primary action at 200%. C offers a better-sized preview but hides privacy; B exposes tools well but its editorial content costs too much space when enlarged. Why B makes the explanation and evidence status easiest to scan; A is a close alternative for uninterrupted reading with fewer disclosure interactions. Scores use A=mean(hierarchy, typography, surfaces), F=mean(clarity, feedback, accessibility), overall=0.4A+0.6F. Component tuples follow the same six dimensions; N/A excludes genuinely inapplicable dimensions from any component average. Feedback scores describe visible state/availability/uncertainty communication and explicitly supplied behavior, never imagined loading, recovery or transitions. Prototype Share scores assess proposed composition: if treated as delivered export products, their blocked Download task would cap their overall grades at 4. The baseline has stronger implementation evidence even though A has the preferred composition. No candidate meets the authorized requirement of A>=9 and F>=9 for every screen and meaningful component.
limitations: Independent read-only assessment used only the four attached screenshot sheets and the evidence boundaries supplied in the prompt. No source, previous scores, history or other graders were inspected.
Initial views do not establish whether lower content is missing or unreachable. Scrolling and disclosure costs were assessed without treating below-fold evidence as deleted.
No runtime checks were performed. Baseline browser, image-export and error-handling evidence is user-supplied; alternatives remain prototypes with no downloaded file and placeholder outbound tools.

Decorative orb imagery does not require an interaction score. Preview text remains small at 200% because the raster artifact itself does not enlarge like surrounding text; an accessible equivalent and a way to inspect the exported image need verification.

Screenshots do not establish measured contrast, 44pt targets, focus behavior, screen-reader semantics, motion preferences, loading/error/empty states or transition stability. Component accessibility scores are visual and provisional.

No real-phone or physical assistive-technology checks were supplied. No 9/10 certification or completed acceptance loop is claimed; the required action/result, state and device evidence remains incomplete.
All candidates display the same supplied reading. Scores address presentation and evidence communication, not model quality or predictive accuracy.
